issues.legal_issue: A family manager may agree to alienate joint family property without legal necessity only where the transaction is shown to confer, or be reasonably expected to confer, a benefit on the family when made.
material_facts: The manager agreed to sell the family’s fractional share of land to a person who already owned most of the land.
There was no legal necessity for the sale.
The claim that the sale benefited the family rested on the small size of its fractional share and the higher price offered than the land’s earlier value.
The pleadings and evidence did not show that the manager considered the property difficult to manage, that retaining it caused loss, or that the proceeds would be invested profitably.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was not established to be for the benefit of the family and was not binding on the family.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, a family manager may alienate joint family property for the family’s benefit even if the transaction is not defensive and there is no compelling necessity. Whether a transaction benefits the family depends on the facts and circumstances, and the court must be satisfied from the material that it conferred or was reasonably expected to confer a benefit when entered into. The Court considered Jagatnarain v. Mathura Das, Hanooman Persaud Pandey v. Babooee Munraj Koonwaree, Sahu Ram Chandra v. Bhup Singh, Palaniappa Chetty v. Sreemath Daiyasikamony Pandara Sannadhi, Sital Prasad Singh v. Ajablal Mander, In the matter of A. V. Vasudevan & Ors. Minors, and Sellappa v. Suppan.

rule.if: manager_contract_to_sell_joint_family_property and no_legal_necessity and family_benefit_claimed and benefit_not_established_at_transaction

predicates.manager_contract_to_sell_joint_family_pr: A family manager agreed to sell property belonging to the joint family.
predicates.no_legal_necessity: The family had no legal necessity requiring the property to be sold.
predicates.family_benefit_claimed: A party claimed that the proposed sale would benefit the family.
predicates.benefit_not_established_at_transaction: The material did not establish that the sale conferred or was reasonably expected to confer a family benefit when it was made.

issues.definition: When a manager agrees to sell joint family property without legal necessity, and the claimed family benefit is not established as a benefit at the time of the transaction, the property is not bound by the sale.

issues.legal_issue: A family manager cannot bind joint family property to a sale justified only by alleged family benefit when adult family members oppose the sale and were not consulted about it.
material_facts: The manager’s brothers were adult members of the family when he agreed to sell the family property.
The adult members opposed the purchaser’s claim and resisted specific performance.
There was no allegation that the adult members agreed to, were consulted about, or knew of the transaction.
issues.conclusion: The adult members were entitled to resist the sale, and the manager could not bind the family property on the ground of alleged benefit without consulting them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that, where adult members of a joint family exist, a proposed transaction for the family’s benefit is not solely the manager’s judgment; the adult members must be involved. It referred to Sital Prasad Singh v. Ajablal Mander, which recognized that adult members with the necessary information may determine that a proposed transaction benefits the estate.

predicates.manager_contract_to_sell_joint_family_pr: A family manager agreed to sell property belonging to the joint family.
predicates.transaction_justified_by_alleged_family_: The proposed sale was sought to be justified on the ground that it would benefit the family.
predicates.adult_family_members_opposed_sale: Adult members of the family resisted the proposed sale.
predicates.adult_family_members_not_consulted: The adult family members were not consulted about the transaction.

issues.definition: If a manager’s proposed sale is justified by alleged family benefit, but adult family members oppose it and were not consulted, the sale cannot bind the family property on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance may be refused where a sale agreement does not bind the family property and the purchaser does not seek partial performance against the contracting manager’s interest.
material_facts: The purchaser sued for specific performance of the manager’s agreement to sell a share of joint family property.
The courts found no necessity for the sale and no established benefit to the family, and adult family members resisted the claim.
The purchaser did not claim that he was willing to pay the entire consideration for a decree limited to the manager’s own interest in the property.
The purchaser did not seek the partial-performance relief described in section 15 of the Specific Relief Act.
issues.conclusion: The courts below were justified in refusing specific performance, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance is discretionary. Section 15 of the Specific Relief Act permits a court, in the circumstances it describes, to order performance of the part of a contract that the defaulting party can perform if the plaintiff relinquishes further performance and the relevant claim to compensation. The Court noted that the purchaser had made no such claim for performance limited to the manager’s interest.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_of_specific_performa: A purchaser appealed after a court refused specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.manager_contract_does_not_bind_family_pr: The manager’s agreement did not bind the joint family property.
predicates.purchaser_did_not_seek_partial_performan: The purchaser did not seek a decree limited to the interest the contracting manager could convey.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal of specific performance, the manager’s agreement does not bind the family property, and the purchaser did not seek performance limited to the manager’s own interest, specific performance is refused.
